bull.b: With no reported debt, Coya avoids mandatory interest payments and refinancing exposure, preserving financial flexibility while its programs advance. This cleaner capital structure can help management direct available resources toward clinical development rather than servicing borrowings.

Reaching 100 enrolled patients in the pivotal ALS study demonstrates continued execution of a major value-driving program. Progress toward full enrollment should bring the company closer to an important clinical readout and a clearer assessment of COYA 302.

Applying Treg biology across ALS and frontotemporal dementia gives Coya an opportunity to extend one therapeutic approach across related neurodegenerative conditions. COYA 303 also broadens the pipeline through a distinct immunomodulatory combination.

bear.b: The scale of operating losses shows that Coya has not yet demonstrated a sustainable earnings model, despite reported top-line growth. Continued losses can consume capital, reduce resilience, and leave future financial performance highly dependent on successful program advancement.

Consistently negative operating and free cash flow means the business is not currently funding development internally. Unless cash burn moderates, Coya will likely need additional financing or partner support to maintain its pipeline and reach key clinical milestones.

Because Coya lacks an approved product-sales base, its revenue capacity depends on collaborations, licensing income, funding, milestones, or eventual royalties. That model can make cash inflows uneven and leaves durable commercial validation dependent on development success.
